reply_text:
Opening the Yahoo/Business Insider page with my last page opening.I found two 2021 forecasts from Sam Altman that aren't recorded yet. Both are in his own essay, "Moore's Law for Everything" (16 March 2021), which I opened in full. A third forecast, from a September 2021 tweet, I could not verify, so I haven't listed it as a candidate.

- **New candidate 1:** right after the two recorded claims, the essay says "in the decades after that, they will do almost everything". The time frame is open-ended ("the decades after that"), so you should decide whether it meets the dating rule.
- **New candidate 2:** "The technological progress we make in the next 100 years will be far larger than all we've made since we first controlled fire and invented the wheel." It sits in the essay's "The AI Revolution" section, but the sentence is about technology in general rather than AI by name, so it's borderline.
- **Already recorded:** the same paragraph contains both recorded claims (five years: legal documents and medical advice; next decade: assembly-line work and companions). The essay's $13,500-per-adult figure is an economic forecast, so I left it out.
- **Unverified, 9 September 2021:** a tweet thread headed "Technology prediction for the 2020s" (x.com/sama/status/1436028666887086104 and …668082462748) appears to say that by 2030 it will be clear AI will push the cost of intelligence towards near-zero. X pages wouldn't open, and the Yahoo/Business Insider write-up couldn't be reached. I saw the words only in search snippets, so I don't quote them. Benzinga's write-up (benzinga.com/news/23/12/36381266/…, not opened) is the most direct way to check it.
- **Not reached:** the New York Times transcript of the June 2021 Ezra Klein interview wouldn't open (both direct and through LessWrong's redirect), so it hasn't been checked for dated claims.
